by: the authoritative verification suite, whose output is the only completion signal
check.freshness: a verdict stands until the code changes or a fix is applied
check.refusal: the loop reports no completion until the suite passes, and stops at its iteration bound with the residue reported
check.observation: none: compliance is decided on the suite's output
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the suite's output, which a completion claim cites

records.title: Verification Loop

exemplar.before: A one-shot fix attempt, unverified — some violations remain, and neither the developer nor the model notices.
exemplar.after: init → verify → classify failures → fix → re-verify → repeat until pass or iteration limit

records.intent: Initialize verification context, execute the verification suite, classify failures, remediate violations, and repeat until pass or iteration limit.
records.invariant: Architectural compliance is achieved through bounded verify-classify-fix cycles, not one-shot remediation.

records.title: Context Initialization

exemplar.before: Failures interpreted with no known rule context, so fixes miss the point.
exemplar.after: discover architecture docs + design guidance → init result containers + iteration counter + max attempts

records.intent: Discover architecture documents, load design guidance, initialize result containers, set iteration counters, and define maximum remediation attempts.
records.invariant: Verification requires a known rule context before failures can be interpreted.

records.title: Verification Execution

exemplar.before: Compliance asserted from confidence, not from the verifier's output.
exemplar.after: run verification suite → capture raw output → parse errors + warnings → pass = errors.length == 0

records.intent: Run the configured verification procedure, capture raw output, parse errors and warnings, and derive pass status from zero-error condition.
records.invariant: Compliance status must be based on executable verification output, not inferred confidence.

records.title: Early Success Exit

exemplar.before: A clean verification result still triggers unnecessary remediation.
exemplar.after: parsed result → is pass? → report zero-violations success and terminate, no mutation

records.intent: If verification has no errors, report successful compliance and terminate without remediation.
records.invariant: A clean verification result is terminal and must not trigger unnecessary mutation.

records.title: Violation Classification

exemplar.before: Errors fixed by ad hoc text editing, not by their semantics.
exemplar.after: each error → category{file_limit | import | naming | base_class | css_token | dom_factory | console | lifecycle} → matching strategy

records.intent: For each verification error, classify the violation into a known remediation category and attach the matching strategy.
records.invariant: Fixes must be selected by violation semantics, not by ad hoc text editing.

records.title: Severity-Ordered Remediation

exemplar.before: A cosmetic warning fixed before a structural blocker.
exemplar.after: classified violations → group by category → order by severity → fix highest architectural risk first

records.intent: Group classified violations by category, order groups by severity, and apply fixes from highest architectural risk to lowest.
records.invariant: Remediation should resolve structural blockers before cosmetic or secondary violations.

records.title: Iteration Bound

exemplar.before: Automated remediation loops forever on an unfixable violation.
exemplar.after: increment iteration → compare to max → {continue | stop, manual review required}

records.intent: Increment iteration count before remediation, compare it to the maximum allowed attempts, and stop with partial success when the bound is exceeded.
records.invariant: Automated remediation must be bounded to avoid infinite repair loops.

records.title: File-Scoped Fix

exemplar.before: A fix edits broadly, breaking things the verifier didn't flag.
exemplar.after: violation → read file → analyze → transform per design guidance → write updated content

records.intent: Read the violating file, analyze the violation type, transform content according to design guidance, write the updated content, and preserve compatibility with verification rules.
records.invariant: Each fix is a localized transformation constrained by architectural guidance.

records.title: File Limit Remediation

exemplar.before: An oversized file trimmed by deleting code instead of splitting responsibility.
exemplar.after: oversized file → split responsibilities into compliant artifacts → preserve imports/exports → rewire references → size <= limit

records.intent: When a file exceeds the allowed size, split responsibilities into smaller compliant artifacts, preserve imports and exports, and rewire references.
records.invariant: Size violations usually indicate excessive responsibility concentration.

records.title: Import Boundary Remediation

exemplar.before: A cross-boundary import error silenced without restoring the boundary.
exemplar.after: invalid import → boundary rule{same-module | shared | adapter} → approved path → rewrite → verify dependency direction

records.intent: Detect invalid cross-boundary imports, locate the approved dependency path or shared abstraction, rewrite imports, and verify dependency direction.
records.invariant: Import fixes must restore architectural boundaries rather than merely silence errors.

records.title: Naming Convention Remediation

exemplar.before: A file renamed but its references left dangling.
exemplar.after: invalid name → naming rule → compliant identifier → rename → update all references (identity migration)

records.intent: Compare file, folder, class, or symbol names against naming rules, derive compliant names, rename artifacts, and update all references.
records.invariant: Naming remediation requires identity migration, not isolated renaming.

records.title: Base-Class Compliance Remediation

exemplar.before: A class missing its required base 'fixed' by silencing the rule.
exemplar.after: class role → expected base → refactor inheritance/composition → migrate duplicated lifecycle into hooks → verify behavior represented

records.intent: Detect classes missing required base abstraction, refactor inheritance or composition according to role rules, migrate duplicated lifecycle logic into hooks, and verify behavior remains represented.
records.invariant: Base-class violations are architectural adoption failures.

records.title: CSS Token Remediation

exemplar.before: A hardcoded color left in place, the rule disabled instead.
exemplar.after: hardcoded style value → resolve design token{existing | new | manual review} → replace → style validation

records.intent: Replace hardcoded style values with approved design tokens, verify token availability, and run style validation.
records.invariant: Presentation constants should resolve through design-system tokens.

records.title: DOM Factory Remediation

exemplar.before: Direct document.createElement kept, the rule ignored.
exemplar.after: direct DOM{querySelector, createElement, innerHTML, direct event} → approved creation boundary → factory rewrite → lifecycle check

records.intent: Replace direct DOM manipulation with the approved DOM factory, component factory, or rendering abstraction.
records.invariant: DOM creation must flow through the sanctioned construction boundary.

records.title: Console Usage Remediation

exemplar.before: A console.log left in and the rule bypassed.
exemplar.after: console call → logger severity mapping{log→info, warn→warn, error→error} → replace → verify no direct console remains

records.intent: Replace direct console calls with the approved logging abstraction, preserve severity and message context, and verify no direct console usage remains.
records.invariant: Observability should be centralized behind a logging contract.

records.title: Lifecycle Symmetry Remediation

exemplar.before: A resource acquired with no release path, leaking.
exemplar.after: lifecycle violation → acquired resources → add destroy/teardown → verify created == destroyed

records.intent: Detect resources created without corresponding cleanup, add destroy or teardown paths, and verify create/destroy symmetry.
records.invariant: Lifecycle compliance requires every acquired resource to have a release path.

records.title: Stylelint Post-Fix

exemplar.before: The next architectural cycle runs on style-broken code.
exemplar.after: remediation → run style validation → fix style errors → block re-verification until style passes

records.intent: After remediation, run style validation, parse style errors, apply style-specific corrections, and block re-verification until style checks pass or are reported.
records.invariant: Syntax and style conformance must be restored before the next architectural verification cycle.

records.title: Reverification Gate

exemplar.before: Local corrections trusted as global compliance.
exemplar.after: fixes applied → local validation → rerun the full authoritative verification suite

records.intent: After fixes and style validation, rerun the full verification suite rather than trusting local corrections.
records.invariant: Only the authoritative verification suite can confirm global compliance.

records.title: Partial Success Reporting

exemplar.before: Iteration bound hit and the run silently reports success.
exemplar.after: max iterations → remaining violations categorized → mark result manual-review-required (visible, actionable residue)

records.intent: When iteration bounds are exhausted, report remaining violations, categorize unresolved issues, and mark the result as requiring manual review.
records.invariant: Bounded automation should fail visibly with actionable residue.

records.title: Completion Report

exemplar.before: A report that mixes fixed violations with tolerated warnings.
exemplar.after: final state → {total iterations, fixed count, remaining warnings, final status{passed | partial | failed}}

records.intent: Report total iterations, fixed error count, remaining warnings, and final verification status.
records.invariant: Completion output should separate fixed violations from tolerated or remaining warnings.

records.title: Codebase Verification Kernel

exemplar.before: Compliance claimed after one edit, never re-verified.
exemplar.after: context → verify → parse → pass? → classify → severity-order fix → style validate → reverify → repeat until zero errors or bound

records.intent: Load compliance context, run verification, parse results, exit on pass, classify violations on failure, remediate by severity, run post-fix style validation, and repeat until zero errors or iteration limit.
records.invariant: Codebase verification is a bounded remediation state machine driven by authoritative compliance output.

records.title: <Compliance Verification Concern>
records.intent: <Load rules> → <Run authoritative verifier> → <Parse failures> → <Classify by violation type> → <Apply bounded fixes> → <Run local post-fix validation> → <Rerun verifier> → <Exit on pass or bound>
records.invariant: Any programmatic compliance workflow should be treated as a bounded verification-remediation loop whose only completion signal is the authoritative verifier passing.
